summary: PulseGuard v0.6.34 is a focused reliability and UI-polish update based on the v0.6.33 real-machine test. It fixes WinGet table parsing and PowerShell 5.1 collection handling, keeps final report serialization off the WinForms UI thread, resolves repaired Windows Repair warnings correctly, cleans native console control-code artifacts, and removes the remaining Optimize-page bottom clipping.

sections.heading: WinGet known-version upgrades are parsed reliably
sections.detail: PulseGuard now derives WinGet table columns from WinGet's own header instead of depending on a fragile spacing regex, with a package-ID fallback for future formatting changes. Known upgrades such as Webex and iCUE are no longer misreported as zero candidates when the table visibly lists them.

sections.heading: WinGet verification is PowerShell 5.1 safe
sections.detail: Per-package results use concrete arrays during post-update verification instead of coercing a generic List[object] through @(...), eliminating the Windows PowerShell 5.1 'Argument types do not match' failure. Known-version packages are still attempted independently and re-inventoried after each update pass; unknown-version packages remain review-only.

sections.heading: Final report generation no longer freezes the interface
sections.detail: FIX + OPTIMIZE no longer performs deep consolidated JSON serialization on the WinForms UI thread after the final CPU measurement. The automatic Full Health worker receives the completed optimization context, creates the fresh post-fix scan, writes the consolidated report in the hidden worker process, and returns only the completed report path/results to the UI.

sections.heading: Windows Repair status reconciles after successful verification
sections.detail: An early Windows Repair warning no longer leaves the Optimize process group yellow after a later DISM/SFC repair and independent integrity verification proves the current state healthy. Component-store IMPROVED/VERIFIED outcomes are likewise treated as resolved advisory maintenance rather than a permanent warning.

sections.heading: Visible maintenance console output is cleaner
sections.detail: PulseGuard strips presentation-only ANSI/CSI erase-line sequences from native maintenance output before displaying/logging it, preventing stray fragments such as '[2' from appearing around SFC/DISM results while preserving the actual diagnostic text and exit result.

sections.heading: Optimize page bottom clipping is corrected
sections.detail: The Optimize workspace now uses deterministic dock sizing for the bottom progress/result bar, disables the AutoScroll interaction that could clip a docked footer, and manually sizes the live-details card above the footer without a competing Bottom anchor. This keeps the live progress text and cleanup details fully inside the page when maximized and under DPI scaling.

sections.heading: Storage optimization behavior is unchanged and media-aware
sections.detail: PulseGuard continues to use Windows defrag.exe /O. Windows chooses the correct operation for each volume: SSD/NVMe volumes receive retrim/optimization rather than a traditional hard-drive defragmentation pass. Partial volume failures remain REVIEW rather than success.
